instructions: When creating a new Word document, read the docx-js.md file completely from start to finish without setting any range limits before proceeding with document creation.
Create a JavaScript/TypeScript file using Document, Paragraph, and TextRun components when creating a new Word document.
Export the new document as .docx using Packer.toBuffer().
When editing an existing Word document, read the ooxml.md file completely from start to finish without setting any range limits before proceeding with editing.
Unpack the document using the command: python ooxml/scripts/unpack.py <office_file> <output_directory>
Create and run a Python script using the Document library to edit the document.
Pack the final document using the command: python ooxml/scripts/pack.py <input_directory> <office_file>
When using the redlining workflow, convert the document to markdown with tracked changes preserved using the command: pandoc --track-changes=all path-to-file.docx -o current.md
Identify and group all changes needed into logical batches of 3-10 related changes.
When locating changes in XML, use section/heading numbers, paragraph identifiers, grep patterns with unique surrounding text, or document structure; do not use markdown line numbers.
Read the ooxml.md file completely from start to finish, paying special attention to the Document Library and Tracked Change Patterns sections, before implementing tracked changes.
Unpack the document using the command: python ooxml/scripts/unpack.py <file.docx> <dir>
Note the suggested RSID provided by the unpack script for use in tracked changes.
Implement changes in batches of 3-10 related changes, grouping them by section, type, complexity, or sequential order.
For each batch, grep for text in word/document.xml to verify how text is split across <w:r> elements.
Use get_node to find nodes, implement changes, then call doc.save() for each batch of changes.
Always grep word/document.xml immediately before writing a script to get current line numbers and verify text content.
After all batches are complete, pack the document using the command: python ooxml/scripts/pack.py unpacked reviewed-document.docx
Convert the final document to markdown for verification using the command: pandoc --track-changes=all reviewed-document.docx -o verification.md
Verify all changes were applied correctly by grepping for original phrases (should not find them) and replacement phrases (should find them) in the verification markdown.
Check that no unintended changes were introduced during the redlining process.
When implementing tracked changes, only mark text that actually changes and break replacements into unchanged text plus deletion plus insertion plus unchanged text.
Preserve the original run's RSID for unchanged text by extracting the <w:r> element from the original and reusing it.
To convert documents to images, first convert DOCX to PDF using the command: soffice --headless --convert-to pdf document.docx
Convert PDF pages to JPEG images using the command: pdftoppm -jpeg -r 150 document.pdf page
When generating code for DOCX operations, write concise code and avoid verbose variable names, redundant operations, and unnecessary print statements.

Install required dependencies if not available: pandoc via sudo apt-get install pandoc, docx via npm install -g docx, LibreOffice via sudo apt-get install libreoffice, Poppler via sudo apt-get install poppler-utils, and defusedxml via pip install defusedxml.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Inspect quarterly_report.docx structure: styles and paragraphs."""
import zipfile
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

SRC = "quarterly_report.docx"
OUT = "inspect_output.txt"
W = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main"


def q(tag):
    return "{%s}%s" % (W, tag)


lines = []
with zipfile.ZipFile(SRC, "r") as z:
    lines.append("== Archive entries ==")
    for n in z.namelist():
        lines.append("  " + n)

    try:
        root = ET.fromstring(z.read("word/styles.xml"))
        lines.append("\n== Styles (styleId -> name) ==")
        for st in root.findall(q("style")):
            sid = st.get(q("styleId"))
            name_el = st.find(q("name"))
            name = name_el.get(q("val")) if name_el is not None else ""
            lines.append("  %s -> %s" % (sid, name))
    except KeyError:
        lines.append("\nNo styles.xml")

    try:
        doc = ET.fromstring(z.read("word/document.xml"))
        lines.append("\n== Paragraphs (index: pStyle | text | first-run fmt) ==")
        for i, p in enumerate(doc.iter(q("p"))):
            ppr = p.find(q("pPr"))
            style_id = None
            if ppr is not None:
                ps = ppr.find(q("pStyle"))
                if ps is not None:
                    style_id = ps.get(q("val"))
            parts = []
            for t in p.iter(q("t")):
                parts.append(t.text or "")
            text = "".join(parts)
            rpr_info = ""
            first_r = p.find(q("r"))
            if first_r is not None:
                rpr = first_r.find(q("rPr"))
                if rpr is not None:
                    attrs = []
                    for child in rpr:
                        tag = child.tag.split("}")[-1]
                        val = child.get(q("val")) or child.get(q("color")) or ""
                        attrs.append(tag + (":" + val if val else ""))
                    rpr_info = " [" + ",".join(attrs) + "]"
            lines.append("  %3d | %-12s | %s%s" % (i, style_id, text[:90], rpr_info))
    except KeyError:
        lines.append("\nNo document.xml")

with open(OUT, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write("\n".join(lines))
print("wrote %d lines to %s" % (len(lines), OUT))
